description_full: Mercedes-Benz Group AG operates as an automotive company in Europe, Germany, North America, the United States, Asia, China, and internationally. It operates through Mercedes-Benz Cars, Mercedes-Benz Vans, and Mercedes-Benz Financial Services segments. The company develops, manufactures, and sells cars and vans under the Mercedes-Benz, Mercedes-AMG, Mercedes-Maybach, G-Class brands, as well as related spare parts and accessories. It also provides financing, leasing, vehicle subscription and rental, fleet management, insurance, and digital services related to charging electric vehicles. The company was formerly known as Daimler AG and changed its name to Mercedes-Benz Group AG in February 2022. Mercedes-Benz Group AG was founded in 1886 and is headquartered in Stuttgart, Germany.

financial_summary: Mercedes Benz Group AG is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $43.9B market cap on $147.3B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -2% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding. Operating margins are contracting by -2.7pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.

Returns on capital run at 7% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 21% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $9.2B in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.50× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.2× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage of 12× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 11.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 20% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
